title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Optical Inspection Station. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Optical Inspection Station
options.lineage: industrial optical comparators & QC inspection benches
options.thesis: VLM proposes, human inspects: every box passes over the comparator glass to be accepted, fixed, or rejected into gold.
options.viewport: Review tab as an inspection bench: the image sits huge under a crosshair reticle left, a frame queue rail with accept/reject lamps runs down the right, stamp actions sit under the glass.
options.risk: Reads as skeuomorphic cosplay if the lamps and stamps decorate instead of carrying real state.

raised.raise: Queue and training metrics render as fixed-cell monospace readouts with amber/red row-lamp state.
Explicit BROWSE/FIX duality: any box is one keypress from editable, corrections land in gold in place.
One type size per role across the whole surface; rank is carried by weight and case, never new sizes.

options.label: Annotation Light Table
options.thesis: A dark neutral bench where the image is the only bright thing; chrome recedes, boxes float on glass.
options.viewport: Full-bleed canvas with the current image lit center, translucent tool tray floating left, filmstrip along the bottom.
options.risk: It is exactly what every annotation tool already ships; nothing here would surprise its user.

options.label: HyperCard Stack
options.thesis: Browse and author are the same object: every screen of the pipeline is editable in place, one painted button from the next.
options.viewport: Each pipeline stage is a card; images are black-and-white cards linked by visible buttons; back retraces your trail.
options.case: Fuses beautifully with our never-mutate-llm/edit-in-place principle; loses clarity because one-bit color cannot carry class-coded boxes.
options.risk: Retro-novelty swamps utility once annotators hit box 500.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: Images, runs, and metrics live as rows on one clacking board whose flaps cascade when anything changes.
options.viewport: One ruled board: every ingested image and training run is a row with flip-character counters and amber delay lamps.
options.case: Superb clarity for the dashboard half of the product; weak identification for hands-on box editing.
options.risk: Per-character flips turn noisy when the queue holds a thousand images.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1971 pocket airline timetables on a light table
options.viewport: Stages as raked glass slides along one lateral rail, all set at a single type size.
options.case: Gorgeous discipline, wrong tool: raked containers fight pixel-precise canvas editing.
options.kept: Single type size per role — rank by weight and case only.

options.label: Seedbed Lobes
options.lineage: saturated-field poster systems with floating capsules
options.viewport: A green field owning the viewport with white capsule panels floating above it.
options.case: Marketing energy, laboratory task: detached lozenges undercut sustained precision work.
options.kept: Class color lives in small disc wells, never in labels.

options.label: Mesophotic Descent
options.viewport: Pipeline stages arranged as one vertical descent with a moving thermocline marker.
options.case: A narrative about depth, not a bench for correction; stage-as-scroll hides the queue.
options.kept: One vertical progress axis ruling stage navigation.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.viewport: Interface states presented as named garment silhouettes pulled taut by one control cord.
options.case: No audience identification with cloth mechanics; metaphor outruns the task entirely.
options.kept: A small vocabulary of named states (raw → reviewing → gold) instead of free-form statuses.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What this category ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
